jobs.title: Defensive Program Director
jobs.description:
Oasis Legal Services seeks a thoughtful and strategic leader to cultivate our Removal Defense program and increase access to culturally-responsive representation for low-income lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) immigrants facing deportation. The ideal candidate is excited by service-delivery innovations and undaunted by obstacles. We are excited to hire someone with at least five years of experience representing clients in front of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), and is able to effectively communicate complex legal topics to clients in Spanish and English, without an interpreter or translator. 

REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS

Reports to Director of Programs & Advocacy in Berkeley CA. Supervises two Staff Attorneys in Berkeley CA, and up to two legal interns at a time.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Team Leadership & Program Strategy

Provide overall development and management of the Defensive Program and work with the Director of Programs & Advocacy and team members to set a direction and vision for the program. Responsible for the success of the program and team members, including the program budget, funding deliverables, and policies and procedures.
Collaborate with the Director of Programs & Advocacy, other Program Directors, and other colleagues to coordinate service delivery across programs, ensure clear communication, and maintain high operational standards and quality legal representation for clients within the Legal Team and Programs Department.
Liaise with the Operations Department on information technology and data systems, and with the Development Department on grant deliverable tracking and reporting. Routinely provide Development Team with ideas, feedback, data and client information for grant applications.
Stay up-to-date on external legal, policy, and funding changes and adjust legal strategy and service delivery accordingly to meet the needs of Oasis’ client communities.

Legal Supervision & People Management

Supervise the legal work of other attorneys and legal advocates to ensure they are providing competent legal representation to clients and managing their caseloads effectively and efficiently. This may include co-counseling cases and providing other support as needed.
Assign legal work and administrative tasks to paralegals, legal interns, pro bono attorneys and other volunteers in coordination with the Affirmative Program Director and Director of Programs & Advocacy. Review declarations, motions, and briefs, and observe intakes and hearings.
Serve as the Oasis supervisor for up to three staff members and up to two legal interns at a time. Participate in weekly individual check-ins with these team members to provide ongoing feedback and support, and guide people in developing and executing appropriate advocacy strategies for their new and ongoing cases.
Participate in Legal Team and Management Team meetings. Support effective recruitment and orientation of Legal Team members, create the conditions for people to succeed at Oasis, support them in following Oasis policies and procedures in tandem with the Operations Team, and identify and facilitate training and other professional development opportunities.

Representation of LGBTQ+ Immigrant Clients

Directly represent LGBTQ+ clients: 

–in removal proceedings in front of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR); 
–in appeals in front of the Bureau of Immigration Appeals and the 9th Circuit;
–in affirmative asylum proceedings in front of the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service (USCIS);
–in credible-fear and reasonable-fear interviews and check-ins in front of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE); 
–in habeas proceedings in front of California District Courts; and
–in California State Court for the purposes of obtaining Special Immigrant Juvenile Status predicate orders.
Interview clients about sensitive topics, and communicate complex legal concepts to clients in Spanish and English, so they understand their options, can make informed decisions, and are prepared for hearings. 
Gather information and collect evidence to inform legal research, case investigation, and strategy. Prepare immigration forms, update databases and maintain accurate records.  
Manage relationships with clients, witnesses, and experts, coordinate their efforts, and track deadlines for a large caseload of up to 12 active clients at a time. Work with the Social Services Program to make referrals for collateral issues clients are facing. Respond to inquiries in a timely manner, including from many clients whose cases have already been filed and are pending.

Partnerships & Advocacy 

Seek out opportunities to represent Oasis externally at conferences, workshops, summits, and participate in collaboratives and partnership meetings focused on service delivery to LGBTQ+ and immigrant communities.
Prepare and deliver training to Oasis colleagues, external partners and service providers on topics such as asylum law, trauma- informed representation, and serving LGBTQ+ immigrants, to increase the capacity of the legal community to serve LGBTQ+ immigrants. Develop new training content and resources as needed to help ensure materials anticipate emerging needs and reflect current law and practice.
Engage in outreach to LGBTQ+ and immigrant communities, and speak persuasively about Oasis and our work to potential clients and to other organizations that serve them, so that all eligible community members are aware of Oasis services. 
Participate in Advocacy Team meetings and help create strategies to foster client empowerment and elevate LGBTQ+ immigrant voices. 

Other Responsibilities

Participate in staff, departmental, and team meetings, professional development activities and other required training, annual all-staff gathering, Oasis’ annual celebration, and performance review systems. 
Work collaboratively with all staff members to ensure effective, comprehensive support for clients and to coordinate best practices across teams, departments, and Oasis offices. Represent the organization internally and externally.
All other duties assigned by their supervisor.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR (requirements)

At least seven years of experience as a licensed attorney, including a minimum of five years representing clients in front of EOIR. 
Juris Doctor degree (J.D.), and member in good standing of a state bar and licensed to practice law in the United States.
Supervisory experience, including supervising other attorneys and/or legal advocates with partial or full U.S. Department of Justice accreditation.
Proficient in both English and Spanish languages (spoken and written). Must be able to communicate to clients in Spanish and English, without an interpreter or translator.
Experience creating tools and workflows to manage a large caseload of clients.
Experience working with low-income LGBTQ+ community members. 
Facility with Google Suite, Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Zoom, and macOS, with ability to learn how to navigate other platforms required for work.
Able to communicate in person and via phone, email and video conference, to work at a computer for extended periods of time, and travel to meetings and events. 
Able to provide proof of COVID-19 vaccination, or participate in an interactive process for accommodations.

Oasis Competencies – How You’ll Do the Work

Problem-Solving & Resourcefulness
Communication
Collaboration
Management

Bonus Qualifications

Experience in project management or program leadership
Experience working with incarcerated and/or detained clients
Experience with federal litigation
Language proficiency in Arabic or Portuguese, in addition to English and Spanish

OTHER DETAILS

This is an exempt, full-time role (35 hours per week, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) based at the Oasis Legal Services office in Berkeley CA, with the option to work from home up to two days per week. The work schedule is subject to change based on programmatic needs, and working some evenings, weekends or holidays may be required. Candidates must be located in the San Francisco Bay Area, and able to work in a shared-office environment where there may be ambient noise and overheard conversations. Occasional travel may be required. 

COMPENSATION

Annual salary
is commensurate with years of same-level experience in a similar role, i.e., either $94,000 for a candidate with less than three years of experience as a Legal Program Director, or $100,000 for 3-5 years of experience, or $108,000 for 6-10 years of experience, or $118,000 for 11+ years of experience. Candidates to advance to the final interview will be asked to provide information about their same-level experience in any similar role, if not included in their resume, as the basis for Oasis to calculate a possible job offer within our salary framework.
Paid Time Off:
Flexible paid time off policy (approximately 25 days annually), winter office closure, and 14 holidays per year including quarterly Oasis wellness days. Sabbatical leave after six years.
Employer contributions
to health insurance coverage (medical, dental, vision), group life insurance, Simple IRA retirement account, and Oasis Family Leave.
Pre-tax savings
on commuter benefits and Flexible Spending Accounts for health care and dependent care expenses.

(budget permitting).
Relocation support
may be available for moving to California from another U.S. state or country.

TO APPLY

We want to hear from you! Complete these two steps by Monday, September 14, 2026
, for priority consideration:
Submit your resume and a sample of your legal writing (max. five pages) to hiring@oasislegalservices.org, with the position title and your name in the subject line (example: “Defensive Program Director, Fulano de Tal”)
Fill out this application form: https://forms.gle/wSpzF1WDrNm7gNdT8. . Be sure to respond to these questions:

JOB TITLE: Deputy Director of Underwriting and Lending Operations

DEPARTMENT: Lending

REPORTS TO: Director of Lending Program Operations

SALARY RANGE: $80,769 - $115,000

FLSA: Exempt

About The Center

Founded in 2008, the Center for New York City Neighborhoods, Inc. (the “Center”) is a not-for-profit that promotes and protects affordable homeownership so that all New Yorkers can build strong, thriving communities. With more than 18 years of experience, the Center's work spans direct services, network coordination, and systems-level intervention. It coordinates a citywide network of housing counseling and legal services providers, operates a statewide Homeowner Hub call center, and co-administers approximately $40 million annually in state funding that supports homeowner services statewide. The Center’s mission-driven CDFI, Sustainable Neighborhoods, lends approximately $7 million annually and holds approximately $100 million in net assets as of December 2025. The Center’s work is grounded in collaboration with community-based partners, public agencies, philanthropy, and national leaders in heirs’ property and housing preservation. Through these partnerships, the Center continues to develop scalable, practical solutions that preserve homeownership, stabilize communities, and expand access to economic opportunity.

Position Summary

The Deputy Director of Underwriting and Lending Operations serves as the operational leader of the underwriting function for all Sustainable Neighborhood lending programs. As a member of the department’s management team, the Deputy Director ensures that the underwriting process is efficient, consistent, and aligned with the organization’s mission, credit philosophy, and risk management objectives. Reporting to the Director of Lending Program Operations, this role translates strategic priorities into effective day-to-day execution by overseeing the people, processes, and systems that support successful loan manufacturing and sound portfolio performance.

The Deputy Director provides leadership to a multidisciplinary team of loan originators, loan processors, and underwriters, ensuring that each stage of the lending process is coordinated from application through credit decision. This role fosters strong collaboration across lending, working closely with compliance and the Closing and Servicing team.

This is a full-time, exempt position based in New York, NY. We operate under a hybrid office model, requiring staff to work a minimum of two days per week on site to support collaboration, connection, and impact. Candidates must be able to meet these in-office expectations.

Primary Responsibilities

The Deputy Director is responsible for the following:

Translate departmental and the Center’s lending priorities into operational plans, procedures, staffing practices, and performance expectations.
Provide day-to-day operational leadership of loan origination, processing, and underwriting across Sustainable Neighborhood lending programs, ensuring applications move efficiently and consistently from intake through handoff to closing. Manage workflow priorities, staff capacity, turnaround times, and cross-functional coordination to support timely decisions and a seamless borrower experience
Supervise, coach, and develop a multidisciplinary team of loan originators, processors, and underwriters. Establish clear performance expectations, monitor workloads and productivity, provide technical guidance, and build staff capacity to consistently meet lending and service standards.
Work closely with leadership to develop and implement standardized procedures, operational controls, and best practices that improve loan cycle times, accuracy, accountability, quality, consistency, and the overall borrower experience
Serve as a key resource for resolving complex or escalated loan files, support staff with difficult transactions, and ensure consistency in underwriting practices across all lending programs. Serve as the primary liaison between senior leadership and frontline lending staff.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators for the lending pipeline—including application volume, turnaround times, approval and decline trends, pipeline aging, productivity, and loan quality—to ensure departmental goals and production targets are achieved while maintaining high standards of credit quality, compliance, and operational performance
Contribute to departmental planning, policy implementation, staff development, and continuous improvement initiatives while supporting new lending products, program enhancements, and technology solutions that improve operational effectiveness

Credit and Risk Management

Oversight of credit analysis and underwriting activities across all Sustainable Neighborhood financing programs, ensuring that lending decisions reflect sound financial analysis, prudent risk management, and the organization’s mission to expand equitable access to capital.
Review complex transactions, providing guidance on loan structuring, and supporting Lending leadership in maintaining a balanced and healthy loan portfolio
Works to proactively identify emerging portfolio risks, recommending operational improvements, and promoting consistent application of underwriting policies and procedures throughout the department

Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required
7+ years of experience in commercial, community development, or CDFI lending, with demonstrated success leading underwriting operations and lending professionals
Fluency with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Meet), Salesforce, BytePro
Highly organized and results-driven
Highly skilled at financial analysis, communication, and process management
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Passionate about promoting affordable homeownership and an equitable New York
Demonstrates a growth mindset through resilience, engaging in expansive thinking, and showing curiosity
Works collaboratively by demonstrating the ability to work in teams

Values

Demonstrate Ownership by showing initiative, active problem-solving, being solution-oriented, acting conscientiously, and putting team results above individual accomplishments
Demonstrate Growth Mindset through resilience, humility, engaging in expansive thinking, and showing curiosity and openness to learning
Work collaboratively by demonstrating the ability to work in teams, exhibiting emotional intelligence

Application

You may apply for this position via the Center’s website, cnycn.org.

Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Applicant review will continue until the position is filled. We thank you for your interest in career opportunities with the Center for NYC Neighborhoods. No phone calls, please. Accepting resumes until the position is filled.

Easterseals Wisconsin

.

Since 1926, Easterseals Wisconsin, a registered 501(c)3 organization, has provided a variety of programs to help people with disabilities live independently, become self-sufficient, and enjoy life more fully through their mission of increasing independence, maximizing opportunities, minimizing barriers, and enhancing the quality of life for people with disabilities

Easterseals Wisconsin seeks a visionary, mission-driven leader to serve as its next President / CEO.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the President / CEO provides strategic and operational leadership, executes the policies and directives of the board, provides oversight and direction for a staff of 30+ employees, and furthers the philosophy and objectives of Easterseals Wisconsin in accordance with Easterseals National.

Key responsibilities

Board Governance & Relations
Work closely with the Board of Directors, ensuring the organization’s activities serve the Easterseals mission, strategic priorities, and financial stability.
Promote the integrity and strength of board leadership and clarity of role, governance, and policies.
Serve as liaison to board committees.

Strategic & Executive Leadership
Advance and promote the mission of Easterseals Wisconsin.
Seek new opportunities for service growth in public and private sectors, strategic alliances, and other opportunities to support the mission of the organization.
Collaborate with board and staff to develop and implement strategic plans.
Ensure that budget, staff, programs, and priorities are aligned with the agency’s mission.
Develop and maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, including Easterseals National, public and private agencies, government entities, and other groups with an interest in serving people with disabilities.
Represent Easterseals Wisconsin to a broad range of constituents and the general public.

Operational & Financial Leadership
Hold overall responsibility for organizational operations, hiring program leaders, and managing organizational finances.
Protect and promote financial stability by preparing and controlling the organizational budget.
Ensure fiscal compliance on matters related to Easterseals Wisconsin’s nonprofit status, annual audit, and financial recordkeeping.
Oversee marketing activities, branding strategy, public relations, and communications.
Provide oversight and management of technology, facilities, and capital projects.

Development Oversight
Provide leadership and oversight of development activities.
In collaboration with development staff, set fundraising goals and identify, cultivate, and solicit donations to support the work and mission of Easterseals Wisconsin.
Promote and advocate for Easterseals Wisconsin and its work in fundraising and public functions.

Program Oversight
Monitor programs, ensuring they are meeting goals.

Verrado is a large-scale master-planned community located in Buckeye, Arizona, in the foothills of the White Tank Mountains, 25 miles west of downtown Phoenix. Verrado is governed by three distinct, yet complementary nonprofit entities responsible for maintaining the vision and integrity of the community: Verrado Assembly, Inc., Verrado Community Association, Inc., and Victory District Association, Inc.

Owner / Managing Member

Metro Atlanta, in-field across all Georgia locations

5 Georgia gyms plus portfolio-wide financial ownership across all 9+ gyms in both states

DS Fitness is a multi-unit Burn Boot Camp operator building toward and beyond a nine-gym portfolio across metro Atlanta and Upstate South Carolina. We run a disciplined operating model with a long-term institutional exit in view, and we care about financial rigor, accountability, and repeatable systems.

Target base of $120,000 to $140,000, plus a performance bonus of 20% to 30% of base tied to cluster NOI and the operating scorecard, with on-target earnings of roughly $150,000 to $175,000. Structure is weightable toward variable for the right operator.

·      The performance of the Atlanta cluster: five gyms, the GMs who run them, and the results they put up. You own how these gyms operate and grow.

·       Run the gyms.
Spend real time in the locations, coach your GMs, set the standard, and hold it. Move each GM from “runs the gym” to “owns the P&L.”

Set and hold the bar for member experience and facility standards across the cluster. Your GMs deliver it day to day. You make sure it stays consistent everywhere.
·       Own the number.
You’re accountable for cluster NOI. Drive membership, retention, conversion, and pricing across the gyms, and manage labor as a percentage of revenue.
·       Run a weekly cadence.
A standing operating rhythm and 1:1s on a scorecard, so every GM knows their numbers and you catch problems early.
·       Own the full SOP loop.
Spot the issue, build the fix, write the SOP, roll it out across the gyms, and hold each GM accountable for putting it in place within a set timeframe. Not just writing the playbook, but making sure the playbook actually gets run.
·       Use the data to stay ahead of problems.
Watch the numbers closely to catch issues as they start and correct them before they grow into real ones.
·       Find and stop the leaks.
The systemic ones that quietly cost real money: overstaffing, inefficient class schedules, missed transfers, sloppy promo execution.
·       Build the systems.
Own the SOP library, the reporting, and franchise and HQ compliance, so the cluster runs on numbers everyone trusts and nothing depends on someone remembering a rule. You own that financial backbone.
·       Open and integrate.
Lead the new locations openings and bring them and their teams up to standard. Each opening carries hard targets: presale goals hit by day 60, and at least 300 members within 90 days of grand opening.

Own GM and staff hiring, onboarding, and retention.

·      You know membership or recurring-revenue businesses: churn, retention, conversion, and pricing.
No fitness background required. We welcome strong multi-unit operators from restaurant, retail, hospitality, boutique fitness, or any location-based service business. We’re hiring for the operating discipline.

·      The fitness product.
Not in this role: product standards, pricing strategy, capital, acquisitions, or vision.

·      A trustworthy portfolio reporting layer and scorecard, built and live.

Lead the next chapter of one of Seattle's defining civic institutions.

Friends of Waterfront Park is seeking an accomplished executive leader to help shape the future of Seattle's waterfront, strengthen the organization behind it, and build the partnerships, culture, leadership capacity and financial foundation required for lasting public impact.
· Location: Seattle, Washington
· Reports to: Board of Trustees
· Search led by: ND Leadership Partners, Managing Partner Chris Nguyen

About Friends of Waterfront Park Friends of Waterfront Park is the nonprofit organization responsible for fundraising, stewarding and programming Seattle’s 20-acre Waterfront Park, a new public space stretching along the city’s central shoreline and reconnecting downtown Seattle with Elliott Bay. Working alongside the City of Seattle, Seattle Center, community organizations, cultural partners, philanthropic contributors and neighboring businesses, Friends brings the park to life through free arts and cultural programming, recreation and wellness, community events, public space activation, partnerships and ongoing stewardship. At its core, Friends works to ensure Waterfront Park is more than a physical place: it is a welcoming and inclusive civic gathering space where people and communities can connect with one another, Seattle’s waterfront and the stories and cultures that define the region.

The Opportunity Seattle's Waterfront Park is the product of decades of civic imagination, public investment, philanthropy, community engagement and partnership. Today, twenty acres of renewed public space reconnect downtown Seattle with Elliott Bay and bring together culture, recreation, nature, commerce and community.
With the capital campaign complete and the full park now open, Friends of Waterfront Park is entering a new institutional chapter. The opportunity ahead is to define the organization's long-term role, strengthen its internal and external leadership capacity, deepen civic and regional partnerships and build a durable financial model that sustains a vibrant, inclusive and welcoming waterfront for generations.
The Board seeks a President and Chief Executive Officer who can lead at the intersection of strategy, people, philanthropy, government, community and civic life. Staff emphasized the importance of a leader whose internal presence, communication, and values are as strong and consistent as their external visibility. The successful executive will build trust, communicate consistently, build leadership capacity, foster collaboration and create clarity while representing Friends with confidence across Seattle and the broader region.

The Executive Mandate The President and CEO will lead Friends through its transition from a successful capital campaign and park opening into its next era as an enduring civic institution. The President and CEO will shape strategy, advocate for Friends and Waterfront Park, steward a consequential public-private partnership, and build the financial and organizational foundation required for long-term impact.

Defining Priorities Build the Institution for the Next Era

Partner with the Board and staff to define Friends’ next chapter, establish clear strategic priorities, and strengthen the organizational capacity needed to deliver them. Foster an environment of trust, accountability and collaboration while ensuring the organization has the people, systems and resources to succeed.

Advocate for Friends and Steward a Complex Public-Private Partnership

Strengthen Friends’ position as a civic leader and trusted partner. Navigate government with political sophistication, advocate for the park and the resources needed to sustain it, build coalitions across public, private and community partners, and shape the next Management Agreement with the City.

Build a Sustainable Financial Model

Develop a diversified long-term financial model that strengthens philanthropy and donor engagement while expanding government support, corporate partnerships, grants, earned revenue and other mission aligned resources.
What Success Looks Like The Search Committee will evaluate candidates’ ability to advance the following outcomes:
·      Map a clear strategic direction guided by the Strategic Plan, as well as a focused set of priorities understood across the Board, staff and key partners.
·      Develop a diversified and sustainable financial model that supports public access, programming and long-term stewardship.
·      Cultivate Friends’ inclusive culture, and facilitate communication, growth and accountability among staff and leadership.
·      Deepen Friends’ relationships with key City and civic partners, secure the resources necessary to support the park and establish a successful framework for the next Management Agreement.
·      Ensure Waterfront Park remains a welcoming, vibrant and inclusive civic gathering place while Friends expands its impact and relevance across Seattle and the region.

Executive Competencies and Experience Friends welcomes candidates from nonprofit, public, philanthropic, cultural, higher education, economic development and other mission driven environments. Direct park management experience is not required. The Search Committee will place significant weight on how candidates lead and on the depth of experience they bring navigating complex, public facing organizations. The following competencies reflect the capabilities and experiences most important to success in this role.

Strategic Institution Visionary
[HT1] 
Sets direction and translates complexity into focused priorities, organizational capacity and sustainable execution. Creates the conditions for others to lead effectively.
Civic and Political Navigator

Navigates government and complex civic environments with political sophistication and sound judgment. Advocates effectively for Friends, Waterfront Park and the public resources required to advance their long-term impact.
Coalition and Relationship Builder

Creates alignment among people and institutions with different interests. Earns trust, communicates effectively and mobilizes public, private, philanthropic and community partners around shared outcomes.
Leadership and Talent Developer

Empowers strong leaders, establishes accountability and creates an environment of trust, collaboration, belonging and professional growth.
Financial Steward

Applies strong financial judgment and aligns philanthropy, government investment, partnerships, earned revenue and disciplined resource allocation to advance long term sustainability.
Inclusive and Resilient Change Leader

Leads with cultural humility, curiosity, courage and emotional intelligence. Understands context, makes difficult decisions and brings people through change with clarity and steadiness.
Leading the Next Chapter Friends has built significant community credibility, programming expertise, partnerships and institutional knowledge. The next President and CEO will be expected to understand and build upon those strengths while bringing greater strategic clarity and organizational maturity. The strongest leader will know when to listen, when to preserve what is working and when to move decisively to position Friends for its next era.

Why Friends of Waterfront Park This is a rare executive opportunity at the intersection of civic leadership, public space, arts and culture, community belonging, economic vitality, philanthropy and government.
The next President and CEO will inherit extraordinary momentum, a highly visible public asset, an engaged Board, talented and committed staff and a network of influential partners. They will also have the opportunity to help define the institution that supports the waterfront for decades to come.
For an executive who believes great cities are strengthened through shared public spaces, strong institutions, inclusive workplaces and authentic partnerships, this role offers the opportunity to leave a visible and lasting legacy.

Compensation and Benefits The anticipated compensation range for the President and Chief Executive Officer is
$280,000 - $340,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications. Friends of Waterfront Park offers a comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined by the organization's compensation philosophy and the experience of the selected candidate.

Search Process This search is being conducted by ND Leadership Partners, led by Managing Partner Chris Nguyen, as a retained executive search. Candidates will be evaluated through a structured process designed to assess executive leadership, strategic judgment, cultural competency, people leadership, relationship building, financial stewardship, governance partnership and the ability to lead through complexity and change.
Qualified candidates and referral sources are encouraged to engage with ND Leadership Partners. All expressions of interest will be managed with appropriate discretion and confidentiality throughout the search process.

Full Job Description:
2026-LZF-Director-of-Development-Communications-Job-Description.pdf

The Opportunity:
LZF seeks an experienced and values-aligned fundraising professional to lead its growing philanthropic and engagement activities. Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director of Development & Communications will oversee all aspects of LZF’s comprehensive fundraising program, including annual and major gifts, planned gifts, grants, events, and in-kind donations from individual, foundation, and corporate donors. This person will help to translate organizational strategy into clear and detailed action plans, playing a key role elevating LZF’s thought leadership as well as in the relationship building, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of major individual and institutional donors to increase contributed revenue. The Director of Development & Communications supervises the Development & Communications Coordinator and works closely with LZF’s Board of Directors, development committee members, funders, and other key stakeholders to achieve or exceed The Fund’s annual revenue goals (~$1.4M in FY26). This position also offers invaluable experiences in both grantmaking and philanthropy. 

Key Areas of Responsibility:

Fundraising
Create and execute a comprehensive annual fundraising plan designed to meet and ideally exceed LZF’s annual revenue goals.
Oversee the strategy, planning, and implementation of LZF’s diversified revenue generation strategies, currently including institutional grants, individual donations, planned giving, in-kind contributions, events, and corporate sponsorships.
Strategically identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward all prospects and supporters
Manage LZF’s institutional funding, including maintaining an annual grants calendar, researching and prospecting, writing grant proposals, and submitting grant reports.
Plan and execute various printed and electronic appeals throughout the year, including for signature annual fundraising events The Zakim Light (September), No Show Ball (November), and year-end appeal.
Grow LZF’s new planned giving program launched in fall 2025.
Serve as main point of contact externally for all development inquiries.
Staff LZF’s Development and Communications Committee: co-create monthly meeting agendas with Committee co-chairs and manage associated board fundraising.
Oversee LZF’s donor CRM (Donor Perfect), ensuring timely and accurate data keeping on donor gifts, touch points, and contact information.
Oversee gift acknowledgements and IRS compliance regarding fundraising.

Communications
With the Development & Communications Coordinator, create and execute annual communications plans designed to raise LZF’s visibility, inspire the philanthropic sector, and support fundraising.
Supervise execution of various printed and electronic communications throughout the year, including e newsletters, social media posts, stewardship mailings, case studies, website updates, and targeted campaigns.
Work with ED to translate 30-Year Impact Study Findings into targeted communications, with support from external marketing and communications consultant.
Work with ED to identify opportunities for LZF to represent grassroots organizations in the field and to deepen the organization’s public engagement and thought leadership.

Events
With the Development & Communications Coordinator and Grants & Program Coordinator, plan and execute Annual Awards Ceremony (February), which serves as both a celebration of our newest cohort of grantee partners and a donor stewardship event.
Plan and execute The Zakim Light (September), LZF’s signature annual fundraising event. This event includes a preview event and a silent auction.
As needed, plan and execute upwards of 2 Bridge Builder events annually to share LZF’s learnings with the philanthropic and nonprofit sectors (usually no more than once per year).

Develop and execute a comprehensive development and fundraising strategy to meet company contributed revenue goals, prioritizing major gifts and planned giving, but also including individual giving, corporate sponsorships, foundation and government grants, annual campaigns, special initiatives, and events.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite and Google products and knowledge of constituent relationship management databases.
Excellent organizational and analytical skills and the ability to consistently meet deadlines.

jobs.description:
Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, the Director of Operations is a hands-on builder charged with supporting the design, implementation, and maintenance of the operational infrastructure that enables Safar Partners to scale as an institutional-grade venture firm. The VP of Operations will be a deeply engaged working partner throughout the build, providing direct guidance, institutional knowledge, and strategic oversight at every stage. 

This is not a role where the infrastructure exists and just needs to be maintained. The Director of Operations will step into an active construction effort — partnering closely with the VP of Operations to design SOPs, implement systems, establish governance frameworks, and create the repeatable operational rhythms the firm needs to compete for institutional LP capital and deliver consistent fund performance. The VP of Operations provides the strategic direction and experience; the Director of Operations provides the execution. 

This role is structured with clear growth intent. As the VP of Operations advances into a broader leadership role, the Director of Operations is expected to develop into the VP of Operations position — taking on increasing strategic responsibility over time as operational systems mature and institutional knowledge deepens. 

﻿A. Building Out the Operational Platform 

This is the defining responsibility of the role — in Year 1 and as the foundation for everything that follows.. The Director of Operations is coordination with the VP of Operations will own the execution of the following: 
The development and deployment of a structured audit of existing workflows across deal execution, portfolio monitoring, and Safar outbound communications — identifying gaps, redundancies, and single points of failure in coordination with the VP of Operations 
Oversight of standard operating procedures (SOPs) for all recurring firm activities: deal pipeline management, portfolio reporting, and investment onboarding 
Development of firm-wide operating calendar integrating deal, portfolio, and strategic planning rhythms into a single coordinated framework 
Development and deployment of repeatable templates and checklists for, portfolio reviews, and Safar communications 
Oversight of the use of CRM, project management, and document management tools that enforce process adherence and reduce dependence on any one individual 
Develop centralized operational knowledge base so institutional knowledge is retained and accessible across the organization 
Development of continuous improvement cadence: quarterly process reviews, team feedback collection, and SOP updates reflecting best practices 
Escalation protocols and decision-making frameworks to ensure the right issues reach the right people in a timely manner 
Work closely with the VP of Operations throughout— surfacing design questions, flagging implementation risks, and ensuring the infrastructure being built reflects institutional standards 

B. Firm Operations & Technology 

Support day-to-day operational collaboration across all functional areas; serve as a central operational liaison across investment, finance, HR, IT, and legal/compliance in coordination with the VP of Operations 
Collaborate with HR and IT to develop on onboarding processes ensuring operational setup, system access, and documentation are in place so new hires are functional from day one 
In coordination with IT, support the firm's technology stack as directed by the VP of Operations; contribute to IT roadmap prioritization in alignment with firm strategy 
In coordination with IT, support cybersecurity governance including endpoint protection, access controls, security training coordination (100% annual staff completion), and incident response protocols 

C. Deal Execution Support 

The Director of Operations supports the process definition and auditing around deal execution — ensuring materials, trackers, and process documentation are in place and adhered to— but does not attend Investment Committee meetings or participate directly in IC deliberations. 
Build and maintain repeatable templates for IC memos, and deal pipeline tracking in coordination with the VP of Operations 
Update, as needed, IC memo and due diligence templates semi-annually in coordination with the VP of Operations. 
Ensure consistent intake process and documentation standards are maintained across the deal pipeline 

D. Portfolio Company Oversight 

Support a consistent, efficient cadence for portfolio company engagement in coordination with the VP of Operations and investment team 
Develop Escalation Response processes ensure the VP of Operations and relevant parties are notified within 24 hours of a triggering event 
Ensure portfolio company documentation and reporting templates are maintained as part of the centralized operational knowledge base 

E. Safar Outbound Relations & Brand Signaling Operations 

The Director of Operations supports the VP of Operations in building and maintaining the operational processes that underpin LP relations and brand signaling. This role does not manage LP relationships or lead fundraising activities directly. 
Build, as needed, and maintain the operational infrastructure and documentation that supports LP due diligence — data rooms, reporting templates, and process documentation in coordination with the VP of Operations and Brand Management, and other outbound communication 
Support the VP of Operations and Brand Signaling in developing needed brand signaling processes: maintaining the operational calendar, and ensuring follow-through on deliverables 
Coordinate LP information, request responses across Finance, Legal, and the Investment Team as directed by the VP of Operations; ensure accuracy, completeness, and timely delivery 
Maintain fundraising pipeline tracking and ensure follow-up actions from funnel meetings are assigned and completed 
Identify and surface process improvement opportunities to the VP of Operations to reduce friction in LP-facing workflows 

F. Compliance, Regulatory & Risk Management 

Support the compliance supervisor function in coordination with Finance and the VP of Operations; ensure adherence to all applicable regulatory requirements 
Coordinate with Finance on compliance-related documentation; ensure maintenance of records required for regulatory filings 
Maintain and enforce data security protocols across internal systems and portfolio company interactions 
Support the VP of Operations in executing the compliance staffing transition plan as the firm adds dedicated resources 

Qualifications

A. Required Experience 

5–7 years of progressive operational experience with exposure to venture capital, private equity, financial services, or a comparable institutional environment 
Demonstrated experience in operational roles with direct accountability for process design, cross-functional coordination, and compliance support 
Proven track record of maintaining and improving operational infrastructure — including SOPs, governance frameworks, and technology platforms — in a fast-moving, multi-stakeholder environment 
Strong project and program management capabilities; demonstrated ability to drive multiple concurrent initiatives to completion across functions with different timelines 
Strong analytical skills 

B. Preferred Qualifications 

Prior Operations Manager or equivalent operational leadership role at a registered investment adviser, venture capital firm, or multi-fund private markets manager 
Familiarity with VC/PE technology platforms: Salesforce, Affinity or comparable CRM, fund administration systems, portfolio monitoring tools, and financial reporting platforms 
Prior experience with commercial data management and business intelligence platforms

Canyonlands Field Institute strives to rejuvenate the human spirit through quality, immersive outdoor experiences. Position Overview

CFI is seeking a collaborative, energetic leader to be our new Development Director. Based out of Moab, Utah, this position oversees all aspects of development for CFI, including grant writing, strategic planning, donor relationship management, and fundraising initiatives. In order to offset the costs of program participation for schools and families, CFI has set the goal, that by 2034, it will receive 80% of funding from philanthropic sources. Our new Development Director will help us get there.

This is a high impact position within a small organization. The ideal candidate for this position is a leader experienced in fundraising, donor relations, and team collaboration. Oasis Legal Services seeks a thoughtful and strategic leader to cultivate our Removal Defense program and increase access to culturally-responsive representation for low-income lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) immigrants facing deportation. The ideal candidate is excited by service-delivery innovations and undaunted by obstacles. We are excited to hire someone with at least five years of experience representing clients in front of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), and is able to effectively communicate complex legal topics to clients in Spanish and English, without an interpreter or translator. 

REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS

Reports to Director of Programs & Advocacy in Berkeley CA. Supervises two Staff Attorneys in Berkeley CA, and up to two legal interns at a time.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Team Leadership & Program Strategy

Provide overall development and management of the Defensive Program and work with the Director of Programs & Advocacy and team members to set a direction and vision for the program. Responsible for the success of the program and team members, including the program budget, funding deliverables, and policies and procedures.
Collaborate with the Director of Programs & Advocacy, other Program Directors, and other colleagues to coordinate service delivery across programs, ensure clear communication, and maintain high operational standards and quality legal representation for clients within the Legal Team and Programs Department.
Liaise with the Operations Department on information technology and data systems, and with the Development Department on grant deliverable tracking and reporting. Routinely provide Development Team with ideas, feedback, data and client information for grant applications.
Stay up-to-date on external legal, policy, and funding changes and adjust legal strategy and service delivery accordingly to meet the needs of Oasis’ client communities.

Legal Supervision & People Management

Supervise the legal work of other attorneys and legal advocates to ensure they are providing competent legal representation to clients and managing their caseloads effectively and efficiently. This may include co-counseling cases and providing other support as needed.
Assign legal work and administrative tasks to paralegals, legal interns, pro bono attorneys and other volunteers in coordination with the Affirmative Program Director and Director of Programs & Advocacy. Review declarations, motions, and briefs, and observe intakes and hearings.
Serve as the Oasis supervisor for up to three staff members and up to two legal interns at a time. Participate in weekly individual check-ins with these team members to provide ongoing feedback and support, and guide people in developing and executing appropriate advocacy strategies for their new and ongoing cases.
Participate in Legal Team and Management Team meetings. Support effective recruitment and orientation of Legal Team members, create the conditions for people to succeed at Oasis, support them in following Oasis policies and procedures in tandem with the Operations Team, and identify and facilitate training and other professional development opportunities.

Representation of LGBTQ+ Immigrant Clients

Directly represent LGBTQ+ clients: 

–in removal proceedings in front of the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR); 
–in appeals in front of the Bureau of Immigration Appeals and the 9th Circuit;
–in affirmative asylum proceedings in front of the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Service (USCIS);
–in credible-fear and reasonable-fear interviews and check-ins in front of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE); 
–in habeas proceedings in front of California District Courts; and
–in California State Court for the purposes of obtaining Special Immigrant Juvenile Status predicate orders.
Interview clients about sensitive topics, and communicate complex legal concepts to clients in Spanish and English, so they understand their options, can make informed decisions, and are prepared for hearings. 
Gather information and collect evidence to inform legal research, case investigation, and strategy. Prepare immigration forms, update databases and maintain accurate records.  
Manage relationships with clients, witnesses, and experts, coordinate their efforts, and track deadlines for a large caseload of up to 12 active clients at a time. Work with the Social Services Program to make referrals for collateral issues clients are facing. Respond to inquiries in a timely manner, including from many clients whose cases have already been filed and are pending.

Partnerships & Advocacy 

Seek out opportunities to represent Oasis externally at conferences, workshops, summits, and participate in collaboratives and partnership meetings focused on service delivery to LGBTQ+ and immigrant communities.
Prepare and deliver training to Oasis colleagues, external partners and service providers on topics such as asylum law, trauma- informed representation, and serving LGBTQ+ immigrants, to increase the capacity of the legal community to serve LGBTQ+ immigrants. Develop new training content and resources as needed to help ensure materials anticipate emerging needs and reflect current law and practice.
Engage in outreach to LGBTQ+ and immigrant communities, and speak persuasively about Oasis and our work to potential clients and to other organizations that serve them, so that all eligible community members are aware of Oasis services. 
Participate in Advocacy Team meetings and help create strategies to foster client empowerment and elevate LGBTQ+ immigrant voices. 

Other Responsibilities

Participate in staff, departmental, and team meetings, professional development activities and other required training, annual all-staff gathering, Oasis’ annual celebration, and performance review systems. 
Work collaboratively with all staff members to ensure effective, comprehensive support for clients and to coordinate best practices across teams, departments, and Oasis offices. Represent the organization internally and externally.
All other duties assigned by their supervisor.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR (requirements)

At least seven years of experience as a licensed attorney, including a minimum of five years representing clients in front of EOIR. 
Juris Doctor degree (J.D.), and member in good standing of a state bar and licensed to practice law in the United States.
Supervisory experience, including supervising other attorneys and/or legal advocates with partial or full U.S. Department of Justice accreditation.
Proficient in both English and Spanish languages (spoken and written). Must be able to communicate to clients in Spanish and English, without an interpreter or translator.
Experience creating tools and workflows to manage a large caseload of clients.
Experience working with low-income LGBTQ+ community members. 
Facility with Google Suite, Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Zoom, and macOS, with ability to learn how to navigate other platforms required for work.
Able to communicate in person and via phone, email and video conference, to work at a computer for extended periods of time, and travel to meetings and events.

Problem-Solving & Resourcefulness
Communication
Collaboration
Management

Experience in project management or program leadership
Experience working with incarcerated and/or detained clients
Experience with federal litigation
Language proficiency in Arabic or Portuguese, in addition to English and Spanish

OTHER DETAILS

This is an exempt, full-time role (35 hours per week, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.) based at the Oasis Legal Services office in Berkeley CA, with the option to work from home up to two days per week. Through these partnerships, the Center continues to develop scalable, practical solutions that preserve homeownership, stabilize communities, and expand access to economic opportunity.

The Deputy Director of Underwriting and Lending Operations serves as the operational leader of the underwriting function for all Sustainable Neighborhood lending programs. new_jobs.title: Director of Operations
new_jobs.description:
Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, the Director of Operations is a hands-on builder charged with supporting the design, implementation, and maintenance of the operational infrastructure that enables Safar Partners to scale as an institutional-grade venture firm. The VP of Operations will be a deeply engaged working partner throughout the build, providing direct guidance, institutional knowledge, and strategic oversight at every stage. 

This is not a role where the infrastructure exists and just needs to be maintained. The Director of Operations will step into an active construction effort — partnering closely with the VP of Operations to design SOPs, implement systems, establish governance frameworks, and create the repeatable operational rhythms the firm needs to compete for institutional LP capital and deliver consistent fund performance. The VP of Operations provides the strategic direction and experience; the Director of Operations provides the execution. 

This role is structured with clear growth intent. As the VP of Operations advances into a broader leadership role, the Director of Operations is expected to develop into the VP of Operations position — taking on increasing strategic responsibility over time as operational systems mature and institutional knowledge deepens. 

﻿A. Building Out the Operational Platform 

This is the defining responsibility of the role — in Year 1 and as the foundation for everything that follows.. The Director of Operations is coordination with the VP of Operations will own the execution of the following: 
The development and deployment of a structured audit of existing workflows across deal execution, portfolio monitoring, and Safar outbound communications — identifying gaps, redundancies, and single points of failure in coordination with the VP of Operations 
Oversight of standard operating procedures (SOPs) for all recurring firm activities: deal pipeline management, portfolio reporting, and investment onboarding 
Development of firm-wide operating calendar integrating deal, portfolio, and strategic planning rhythms into a single coordinated framework 
Development and deployment of repeatable templates and checklists for, portfolio reviews, and Safar communications 
Oversight of the use of CRM, project management, and document management tools that enforce process adherence and reduce dependence on any one individual 
Develop centralized operational knowledge base so institutional knowledge is retained and accessible across the organization 
Development of continuous improvement cadence: quarterly process reviews, team feedback collection, and SOP updates reflecting best practices 
Escalation protocols and decision-making frameworks to ensure the right issues reach the right people in a timely manner 
Work closely with the VP of Operations throughout— surfacing design questions, flagging implementation risks, and ensuring the infrastructure being built reflects institutional standards 

B. Firm Operations & Technology 

Support day-to-day operational collaboration across all functional areas; serve as a central operational liaison across investment, finance, HR, IT, and legal/compliance in coordination with the VP of Operations 
Collaborate with HR and IT to develop on onboarding processes ensuring operational setup, system access, and documentation are in place so new hires are functional from day one 
In coordination with IT, support the firm's technology stack as directed by the VP of Operations; contribute to IT roadmap prioritization in alignment with firm strategy 
In coordination with IT, support cybersecurity governance including endpoint protection, access controls, security training coordination (100% annual staff completion), and incident response protocols 

C. Deal Execution Support 

The Director of Operations supports the process definition and auditing around deal execution — ensuring materials, trackers, and process documentation are in place and adhered to— but does not attend Investment Committee meetings or participate directly in IC deliberations. 
Build and maintain repeatable templates for IC memos, and deal pipeline tracking in coordination with the VP of Operations 
Update, as needed, IC memo and due diligence templates semi-annually in coordination with the VP of Operations. 
Ensure consistent intake process and documentation standards are maintained across the deal pipeline 

D. Portfolio Company Oversight 

Support a consistent, efficient cadence for portfolio company engagement in coordination with the VP of Operations and investment team 
Develop Escalation Response processes ensure the VP of Operations and relevant parties are notified within 24 hours of a triggering event 
Ensure portfolio company documentation and reporting templates are maintained as part of the centralized operational knowledge base 

E. Safar Outbound Relations & Brand Signaling Operations 

The Director of Operations supports the VP of Operations in building and maintaining the operational processes that underpin LP relations and brand signaling. This role does not manage LP relationships or lead fundraising activities directly. 
Build, as needed, and maintain the operational infrastructure and documentation that supports LP due diligence — data rooms, reporting templates, and process documentation in coordination with the VP of Operations and Brand Management, and other outbound communication 
Support the VP of Operations and Brand Signaling in developing needed brand signaling processes: maintaining the operational calendar, and ensuring follow-through on deliverables 
Coordinate LP information, request responses across Finance, Legal, and the Investment Team as directed by the VP of Operations; ensure accuracy, completeness, and timely delivery 
Maintain fundraising pipeline tracking and ensure follow-up actions from funnel meetings are assigned and completed 
Identify and surface process improvement opportunities to the VP of Operations to reduce friction in LP-facing workflows 

F. Compliance, Regulatory & Risk Management 

Support the compliance supervisor function in coordination with Finance and the VP of Operations; ensure adherence to all applicable regulatory requirements 
Coordinate with Finance on compliance-related documentation; ensure maintenance of records required for regulatory filings 
Maintain and enforce data security protocols across internal systems and portfolio company interactions 
Support the VP of Operations in executing the compliance staffing transition plan as the firm adds dedicated resources 

Qualifications

A. Required Experience 

5–7 years of progressive operational experience with exposure to venture capital, private equity, financial services, or a comparable institutional environment 
Demonstrated experience in operational roles with direct accountability for process design, cross-functional coordination, and compliance support 
Proven track record of maintaining and improving operational infrastructure — including SOPs, governance frameworks, and technology platforms — in a fast-moving, multi-stakeholder environment 
Strong project and program management capabilities; demonstrated ability to drive multiple concurrent initiatives to completion across functions with different timelines 
Strong analytical skills 

B. Preferred Qualifications 

Prior Operations Manager or equivalent operational leadership role at a registered investment adviser, venture capital firm, or multi-fund private markets manager 
Familiarity with VC/PE technology platforms: Salesforce, Affinity or comparable CRM, fund administration systems, portfolio monitoring tools, and financial reporting platforms 
Prior experience with commercial data management and business intelligence platforms

Canyonlands Field Institute strives to rejuvenate the human spirit through quality, immersive outdoor experiences. We aim to create a world where the people, wildlife, and plants of the Colorado Plateau are healthy and vibrant. As we work toward this vision, we must acknowledge that people and landscape are inexorably connected. We are committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive culture in all that we do. Over the past 40 years Canyonlands Field Institute has build a reputation of excellent in outdoor education for youth and adults, we encourage you to join our team and help us continue to grow!

Position Overview

CFI is seeking a collaborative, energetic leader to be our new Development Director. Based out of Moab, Utah, this position oversees all aspects of development for CFI, including grant writing, strategic planning, donor relationship management, and fundraising initiatives. In order to offset the costs of program participation for schools and families, CFI has set the goal, that by 2034, it will receive 80% of funding from philanthropic sources. Our new Development Director will help us get there.

This is a high impact position within a small organization. The ideal candidate for this position is a leader experienced in fundraising, donor relations, and team collaboration. Candidates must have a strong connection to, and passion for, CFI’s mission is to cultivate connection to self, community, and nature by creating inclusive educational pathways to the outdoors. The ideal candidate is an effective communicator, catalyst, and strategic thinker who is knowledgeable about fundraising best practices and processes.

Lead the development of the annual fundraising and development strategy, ensuring it reflects CFI’s mission.
Cultivate and promote CFI’s core values through development initiatives.
Identify innovative revenue generation strategies and build a diverse funding base, including individual donors, foundations, and other sources.
Cultivate and steward donor relationships to enhance ongoing support.
Ensure regular, proactive donor communication.
Create innovative opportunities to engage donors and sponsors, foster long-term relationships.
Oversee timely and accurate donor acknowledgements and communication tracking in the donor management system.
Lead the prospecting efforts to identify and engage potential individuals, foundations, and other funders.

Supervise the Grant Writer, providing coaching, guidance, and support to help them succeed in their role.

Overview

The Data Program Deputy Director at the Green Mountain Care Board (GMCB) supports the strategic direction, management, and advancement of the Board's data and analytics initiatives. This role helps oversee data governance, ensures high-quality and accessible health system data, and works closely with leadership to drive analytic priorities that inform regulatory and policy decisions. The Deputy Director collaborates across teams, manages complex projects, and contributes to a data-driven culture that strengthens Vermont's health care system.

Who May Apply

This position, GMCB Data Program Deputy Director (State Promotional) (Job Requisition #55621)
, is listed as a STATE PROMOTIONAL ONLY posting. Only current State of Vermont employees who have successfully completed an original probationary period OR non-State employees eligible for veteran's preference are eligible to apply for this position. Your application will not be considered if you do not meet one of these requirements.

If you would like more information about this position, please contact Emily.Brown@vermont.gov.

Resumes will not be accepted via e-mail. You must apply online to be considered.

Class Definition

Serves as the Data Program Deputy Director for the Green Mountain Care Board (GMCB). Responsibilities include assisting the Director in the management, planning, and implementation of strategic, programmatic, and organizational change initiatives, as well as the collection, storage, processing, analysis, and reporting of critical health system data across the institution. Work is performed at a professional level and is focused on assisting the Director in managing the statewide health system data program. This includes the management of large health system data-related processes, systems, assets, and system changes affecting GMCB as an enterprise and for other state agencies requiring health system data products (e.g., Agency of Human Services). Position incumbents support the Director in overseeing the development and implementation of GMCB's enterprise portfolio of data work, practices, and systems. Collaborative work with the Agency of Digital Services is expected. The Deputy will support the Director in developing long-range plans and programs related to GMCB goals and overall policy directives, including ensuring those plans and programs align with federal and state mandatory requirements. Positions at this level work closely with the Director to build Program and project budgets, monitor costs, and facilitate the allocation of resources at the Director's instruction to achieve the change management, health system data process, and technology goals at GMCB. Supervision may be exercised directly over a portion of data staff, and indirectly over the other program staff. Additional staff may also be under the incumbent's supervision contingent upon current health system data and infrastructural projects. Duties include coordinating and collaborating with GMCB and other Program leadership, GMCB Business Offices, State Enterprise Project Management Office, Program managers, and Information Technology Leaders, managers, and staff. Work is performed under the general supervision of the Director.

Environmental Factors

Work is performed in a standard office setting and/or remotely. Some travel may be required for which private means of transportation should be available. Work outside of regular work schedule should be anticipated.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or higher in social science, business or public administration, computer science, or related field AND four (4) or more years of experience in data project management, reporting, and analysis, INCLUDING two (2) or more years of supervisory experience.

OR

Eight (8) or more years of experience in data related project management, reporting, and analysis, INCLUDING two (2) or more years of supervisory experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in social science, business or public administration, computer science, or related field.

Demonstrated experience working on multiple overlapping projects.

Demonstrated experience delivering work products on program deadlines.

People leader experience within a Health system-focused institution.

Experience working in Agile environments.

Experience managing multiple types of problems at the same time.

Experience in Health system technology.

Total Compensation

As a State employee you are offered a great career opportunity, but it's more than a paycheck. The State's total compensation package features an outstanding set of employee benefits that are worth about 30% of your total compensation, including:

80% State paid medical premium and a dental plan at no cost for employees and their families
Work/Life balance: 12 paid holidays each year and a generous leave plan
State Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FMLI)
Two ways to save for your retirement: A State defined benefit pension plan and a deferred compensation 457(b) plan
Tuition Reimbursement
